setup.title: Python interpreter
setup.intro: BluePy runs your code in a regular Python. Python {{minimum}} or newer must be installed.
setup.automaticHint: BluePy picks the newest usable version.

install.title: Install Python
install.win32: Download Python from python.org and tick “Add python.exe to PATH” in the installer. Then restart BluePy.
install.darwin: Download the macOS installer from python.org (not the Python that comes with the Xcode tools). Then restart BluePy.
install.linux: Install your distribution's python3 package (e.g. sudo apt install python3 python3-tk). Then restart BluePy.

welcome.title: Welcome to BluePy

debugger.haltHint: Pauses the running program at its next line

tests.recordIntro: Everything you do with objects now (create, call methods) is written as Python code into the new test method. For return values the result dialog offers an assertion.
tests.recordBenchHint: The object bench is cleared first and filled with the fixture (setUp) of the test class – just like the test will run later.
tests.nameNotTest: Test methods must start with “test”, otherwise unittest does not find them.
tests.noTests: No tests found – test methods are named test_…
tests.empty: No test run yet. Right-click a test class in the class diagram or use “Run Tests”.
tests.selectHint: Click a test for details; double-click opens the source.

hub.settingsIntro: The hub is the server assignments come from and submissions go to. Your teacher gives you the address – teachers also enter their teacher key.
hub.personalHint: The 6-character code from your teacher. BluePy remembers it on this device.
hub.teacherKeyHint: Stored encrypted in the system keychain. Create one on the hub: `python -m bluepy_hub teacher add "Name"`.
hub.fetchHint: Your teacher handed out the code. The assignment goes to Documents/BluePy/Aufgaben and opens right away.
hub.notAssignment: The open project is not a hub assignment. Get an assignment first (Assignments ▸ Get assignment…).
